# Job cards: numbering, status, invoicing, notes and assignees

> Detail split out of CLAUDE.md. Read before touching job numbering, job status, invoicing/archiving, deletion, comments or who is assigned.

## Numbering

**Job card auto-numbering**: Job numbers are auto-generated from two settings: `job_number_prefix` (e.g. `"DH-"`) and `job_number_next` (e.g. `"00001"`). The format preserves leading zeros (width of `job_number_next` string). On each job card creation, the server generates `{prefix}{paddedNumber}`, validates uniqueness, inserts the record, then increments `job_number_next`. Deleted job numbers are never reused (counter only goes forward). The job number field is read-only in the create form. Admin configures prefix and starting number in Settings > Job Card Numbering. If not configured, job card creation is blocked with an error message.

## Work-driven automatic status

**Work-driven automatic status**: A job's status follows the shop floor — it is recomputed from logged work on every work event (timer start/stop, time block added or deleted, finished quantity edited, and — since 2026-09-25 — a part added, changed or removed via `jobcard-items.js`, since a line change also changes what completion needs) by `syncStatusToWork` in `server/src/utils/jobStatusAuto.js`. Rule: every line at (or over) its ordered quantity ⇒ `DONE`; otherwise ⇒ `IN_PROGRESS`. Completion sums the good pieces (`qty`) from **finished** time blocks per line and compares to the line's quantity; a job with no lines, or any line whose quantity is missing/zero, is never complete. This **overrides** a manual status flip: if a manager moves a job elsewhere and a worker then logs work, it snaps back to match reality — to hold a finished job in another state the work itself must change. The only status it never touches is `INVOICED` (terminal); it also no-ops on archived jobs and when the status already matches. It does **not** write its own history row — it returns the `{ from, to }` change (or null) and the calling work route folds it into the history entry it already writes for that work event, so one action shows as one audit row carrying both the work change and the status move. Auto-status failures never break the work action. This is why **quantity is now required and must be a positive whole number** on every line item — it is the completion target. Enforced client-side (`jobCardValidation.mjs`, number input in `ItemsTab.jsx`) and server-side (`validateItemQuantities` in `validation.js`) on create and update. **Every part route's reply carries a top-level `jobStatus`** (the job's status after the write, always — not only when it changed) — `jobcard-items.js`'s add/update/delete all read it fresh off the job row after folding any `syncStatusToWork` change into their own history entry, so the screen can show the job's current status from the same reply without a separate re-fetch, the same way the time routes already let a status move surface without one.

## Invoicing and archiving

**Auto-archive on INVOICED**: When a job card's status transitions to `INVOICED` (via `PUT /:id` or `PATCH /:id/status`), the server automatically sets `archived = 1` and stamps `invoicedDate` with the current timestamp — on **both** routes the status write and the archive write run inside one `db.transaction`, so a failure between them can't leave a job reading INVOICED while still in the open list. Only management can set status to INVOICED. **Invoicing is an update-only transition**: a job is never *created* as INVOICED — the create route (`POST /`) rejects a `status` of `INVOICED` with 400, because only the update/status paths run the auto-archive + missing-files check, so allowing it at creation would strand a job in the invoiced-but-still-open limbo the status-lock exists to prevent. The status picker on the job screen mirrors this (INVOICED is offered only when editing an existing job, never while creating one). There is no manual archive endpoint; unarchive (`POST /:id/unarchive`, management) is the only way to reverse it. **An archived (invoiced/filed-away) job is status-locked**: both status-changing paths refuse any status change while `archived === 1` (returns 409 **before any write**) — `PATCH /:id/status` blocks every status change, and `PUT /:id` blocks a status change while still allowing edits to other fields — so even an admin can't recreate the filed-away-but-OPEN limbo by editing. The lock keys off the `archived` flag alone (invoicing always files a job away; unarchive always clears it). **Unarchive also resets `status` to `OPEN`** (in the same `unarchive` query) so a re-opened job returns as a normal working job rather than a back-in-the-list-but-still-INVOICED contradiction; the reset is recorded in history alongside the `archived`/`invoicedDate` changes.

**Hard running-timer checkpoint**: Both routes that can set status `INVOICED` also refuse **before any write**, and before the soft attachment checkpoint below, when any time entry on the job is still running (`end_time IS NULL`) — 409 `{ error: 'A timer is still running on this job. Stop it before marking the job invoiced.' }`. Unlike the missing-attachments checkpoint this is a hard block with no confirm-anyway body flag: a running timer can't be confirmed away, since invoicing archives the job and an archived job's time can no longer be changed (see `docs/notes/time-and-costing.md`) — stopping it after the fact wouldn't be possible. The same hard refusal covers a **just-stopped block whose worker is still filling in the stop-timer form**: a block on the job stopped within the last 30 minutes that still has no description (the form won't save without one) refuses invoicing with 409 `'Someone has just stopped a timer on this job and is still filling in their pieces. Try again once they have saved it.'` — otherwise invoicing files the job away mid-form and the form's save is refused, losing the pieces, scrap and inspection answers. The 30-minute window means a form someone walked away from never blocks the job for good. Both checks live in one helper, `invoiceBlockedByTime` (`utils/timeEntryHelpers.js`), called from both routes.

**Soft close-out checkpoint**: When `PUT /jobcards/:id` or `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` would set status to `INVOICED` (which also archives) and any attachment gaps exist, the server returns 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_ATTACHMENTS', attachmentWarnings }` **before any write**. The client shows an "Invoice anyway?" confirm and resends with `confirmMissingAttachments: true` in the body to bypass the check. This is a soft nudge, not a hard block.

## Deleting a job

**Soft delete checkpoint**: `DELETE /jobcards/:id` (admin) never deletes on the first request — because deleting is permanent and the job number is never reused, the server always returns 409 `{ error: 'CONFIRM_DELETE', workWarning }` **before any write** unless the body carries `confirmDelete: true`. `workWarning` is `null` when the job has no recorded work (client shows a plain "are you sure"); when any time has been logged or a timer is running (both cascade away on delete) it carries `{ hasActive, activeWorkers, loggedHours, pastWorkers }` so the confirm can name who/what is being erased. The confirmation lives entirely in this one 409 round-trip — there is no separate client-side pre-confirm — so the admin only ever sees a single dialog. Resending with `confirmDelete: true` bypasses the gate. Mirrors the missing-attachments checkpoint.

## Comments (notes)

Notes endpoints: `GET /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated — **newest first**, `created_at DESC` with `rowid` as tie-break), `POST /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/notes/:noteId` (management). The **job list response also carries each job's newest comment** as `latestNote` (`{ text, userName, createdAt }`, or `null`) — fetched for all listed jobs in one pass by `getLatestNotesForJobcards` (`db/queries/operations.js`, a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY jobcard_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC)` pick, i.e. **the same ordering the thread uses**, so the column can never show a different comment than the top of the thread when two share a timestamp; it returns raw rows and the route converts to camelCase at the boundary) and rendered as the **Latest Comment** column sitting between Status and Priority in the job list (full text floats on hover with author + time). Adding or deleting a comment in the job screen hands the newest remaining comment back to the list via `onNotesChange`, which **patches that one row in place** (never a whole-list re-fetch). The column ids `latestNote` and `print` must each exist in **both** `DEFAULT_COLUMN_ORDER` (`JobCardList.constants.js`) and its server mirror `JOBCARD_COLUMN_IDS` (`middleware/validation.js`) — the server validates saved column order/visibility against that list, so a column missing there breaks reordering for everyone. The **Print** column reads `printedAt` straight off each job in the list response (stamped by the print-confirmation route once a packet carrying the job card has actually reached a viewer — see `docs/notes/files-and-qa.md`) and sorts via a getter in `useJobCardSort.js`, the same pattern every sortable column follows. `mergeColumnOrder` folds a newly-added column into a user's saved order at its default position and always keeps `actions` last. The Excel export re-reverses the thread so its Notes cell still reads oldest-first.

## Assignees

Assignee endpoints: `PUT /jobcards/:id` no longer takes `assigneeIds` at all — the branch that reconciled a whole list was stripped in Stage 4b of `tasks/instant-save-job-card.md` once nothing sent it any more (the job screen writes one worker at a time, and `buildJobcardPayload` only puts `assigneeIds` in the **create** payload). `POST /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-assign — uses `req.user.userId`, body ignored), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-unassign). Self routes log history with action `self_assign` / `self_unassign`. `PUT /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId` and `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId` (both management, idempotent, 404 if the user doesn't exist) put or take off **one** worker without touching anyone else's row — the instant-save equivalent of the self routes, for the person ticking names on someone else's behalf. History action `assign` / `unassign`; both keep the same `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE` swallow the self routes use, since a timer auto-assigning the same worker can race the same insert. These are what the job screen's people tiles now call on every tap.

Item endpoints, same instant-save batch (`server/src/routes/jobcard-items.js`, management, wired into the job screen's parts list via `useInstantItems.js`): `POST /jobcards/:id/items` adds one part (no archived-job lock — `PUT /jobcards/:id` deliberately allows editing everything but the status on a filed-away job, and these routes match it); `PATCH /jobcards/:id/items/:itemId` changes one part — absent fields are unchanged, the body is merged over the stored row before validating, and the part never moves position; `DELETE /jobcards/:id/items/:itemId` removes one part (blocked if time is logged against it, or if it's the job's last remaining line). All three run the same seven item validators the create route (`POST /jobcards`) uses, grandfathering values already saved elsewhere on the job, and each names the part in its error message by description rather than position (a one-element validation batch can't report a meaningful array index) — `PUT /jobcards/:id` no longer takes `items` either, so these are now the *only* way an existing job's parts change. **A part's `item_number` is a sort order the server owns, not its identity — its permanent `item:` id is.** A new part gets `MAX(item_number) + 1` for the job, computed inside the same transaction as its insert, so it can never collide with a number picked at the same moment or repeat a gap. **Nothing renumbers on delete** — gaps are expected and fine; the number shown on screen is the part's `position`, a display-only field the **server** states on every part it returns — its 1-based index in that job's parts ordered by `item_number` ascending. A screen never counts this for itself any more (it used to, per-screen, before this field existed) and never sends `position` anywhere or writes it onto a row — identity is always the permanent `item:` id. A one-time startup conversion (`cleanUpDuplicateItemNumbering` in `db/init.js`) folds any job whose numbers still carry **duplicates** from before this change onto a clean 1..n ordering; gaps are left exactly as they are, since closing them on every boot is the very instability this change removed. It runs on every boot and is a no-op once a job has no duplicates. History folds into the job's `update` action, keyed by the part's description (`part "X" added` / `part "X"` / `part "X" removed`) rather than its number, since a part's number is no longer stable enough to identify it across edits; a no-op edit (summary unchanged) writes no history row. Each of the three routes returns the job's full, freshly-recomputed part list (`items`, each carrying its own `position`) and `attachmentWarnings` alongside its own result, the same way the whole-job save already does, so a screen acting on the reply never has to separately re-fetch either.

`PUT /jobcards/:id` itself, after Stage 4b, only ever touches the job's own single-value fields (status, priority, due date, description, PO/quote/previous-job references, quality level, repeat job, photos) plus the invoice-time archive. It takes no `items` and no `assigneeIds` — sending either is simply ignored (an unrecognised body key, same as any other), and the delete-guard against removing a line with logged time now lives solely in `jobcard-items.js`'s own `DELETE` route.
